newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor hopeful on Mozambique aluminium smelter.
newsitem.headline: Gencor hopeful on Mozambique aluminium smelter.

text.p: Gencor Ltd is still hopeful about the development of a planned 245,000 tonnes a year aluminium smelter, chairman Brian Gilbertson said on Tuesday.
Gilbertson told Reuters that a feasibility study into the Mozal smelter near Maputo had been completed and showed that the project was feasible.
"The smelter in Mozambique is an important decision that lies ahead. The feasibility study has been completed which shows that it is perfectly feasible," he said in an interview.

Gencor unit Alusaf Ltd already owns two smelters at Richards Bay in South Africa. Alusaf was a major contributor to Gencor's earnings in the six months to end-December 1996 with 38 percent of the group's operating income.
But Gilbertson said based on present calculations the Mozambique smelter is not yet attractive enough as an investment.
"As we calculated the returns on the capital, it is really not yet attractive enough as an investment.

"But I have authorised some further expenditures for the team to work on it to see if they can try and get the power formula, the capital expenditures, the project timing and so on to try and improve it to what would be acceptable.
"That is a high priority for us," he added.
Gencor has said that the key to a succesful project in Mozambique -- with an estimated capital cost of 4.5 billion rand -- was a long term power contract.
On Tuesday, Gilbertson said Gencor had been offered a power contract by South Africa's Eskom and Mozambique's state electricity utility EDM.
